title: Generalized conditions for odd-frequency pairing in superconducting systems
authors: Florian Kayatz, Annica M. Black-Schaffer, Jorge Cayao
abstract: Odd-frequency superconducting pairing has been predicted to arise in many systems and is known to lead to phenomena such as paramagnetic Meissner response and long-range superconducting proximity effect. Here, we provide generalized necessary and sufficient conditions for odd-frequency pairing appearing in any superconducting system, from bulk superconductors to superconducting hybrid structures. This generalizes an earlier first-order expression in multiband bulk superconductors to all superconducting systems and to all orders, in both order parameter and frequency. We then apply the derived conditions to several systems, including superconducting-ferromagnet and superconducting Josephson junctions, as well as a transition metal dichalcogenide monolayer proximitized by a conventional superconductor, where the generalized conditions are used to understand the properties of the superconducting state.
summary: This work establishes generalized, necessary, and sufficient conditions for odd-frequency superconducting pairing applicable to all superconducting structures. By analyzing various physical systems like SF junctions and TMDs, the authors demonstrate that the non-zero commutator of the normal and superconducting Hamiltonians dictates the presence of this exotic pairing state. This advances the theoretical understanding of unconventional superconductivity signatures.
main_problem: To derive generalized necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of odd-frequency superconducting pairing in any superconducting system.
main_result:
The condition for odd-frequency pairing is found to be the non-zero commutator $[\hat{h}, \hat{\Delta}]^* 
eq 0$, which holds regardless of the order parameter expansion or system complexity.
method: The authors use Green's function theory, employing Neumann series and high-frequency expansions of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian to analyze the anomalous electron-hole Green's functions.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to diverse superconducting systems, including bulk superconductors, superconducting-ferromagnet (SF) junctions, Josephson junctions, and TMD monolayers proximitized by conventional superconductors.
key_observables: Odd-frequency pair amplitudes ($F_{ij}(z)$), paramagnetic Meissner response, and the commutator $[\hat{h}, \hat{\Delta}]^*$.
important_parameters: Superconducting gap ($\Delta$), magnetic field ($b_x$), and various hopping/tunneling amplitudes ($t, t_s, \Delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on expanding the Green's functions in powers of the order parameter ($\hat{\Delta}$) and utilizing high-frequency approximations for computational tractability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the absolute value of the pair amplitude $F_{\uparrow\uparrow}$ versus frequency $z$ for specific couplings (like $t_s$ or $b_z$) in junction models.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the general condition using Green's functions, then applies this condition systematically to model junctions (SF and Josephson) and advanced materials (TMDs) to confirm the theoretical predictions.
why_interesting: The rigorous derivation of a universal condition for odd-frequency pairing provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding unconventional superconductivity, which is a major topic in condensed matter physics.
